papers.title: HDMark: Holographic Multi-Bit Model Watermarking for Intellectual Property Protection in Hyperdimensional Computing
papers.abstract: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) models deployed on edge hardware are valuable intellectual property that is easy to steal, since a trained classifier consolidates its learned knowledge into a compact set of class prototype hypervectors; yet protecting their ownership through watermarking remains largely unexplored. We present HDMark, the first model watermarking framework native to HDC, which encodes ownership in the same hyperdimensional algebra the model computes with. HDMark maps a multi-bit owner identity to secret quasi-orthogonal carriers, superimposes them holographically onto the trained class prototypes, and verifies ownership with a statistical test. Across four datasets and three HDC learning rules, HDMark leaves accuracy essentially unchanged and verifies a 64-bit identity in 99.8% of trials at p < 0.001. We derive closed-form expressions for prediction fidelity and bit recovery that match measurements within 0.4 pp mean absolute error. The watermark survives fine-tuning and low-bit quantization, while attempting to erase it through noise injection, pruning, or overwriting severely degrades model accuracy. We further identify a dimension-permutation attack specific to HDC, which reorders hypervector coordinates to evade verification without altering predictions, and counter it through encoder realignment. Finally, an AMD ZCU104 FPGA implementation confirms that HDMark adds no hardware overhead, remains bit-exact under aggressive undervolting, and stays verifiable under timing faults until the classifier itself fails.

papers.title: AI, Bias, and Inclusion: A Two-Phase Mixed-Methods Study of Gender Bias, Awareness, and Trust in Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are widespread across fields such as healthcare, finance, employment, and criminal justice, with a substantial impact on the lives of individuals and society. However, it has been established that AI systems perpetuate existing social inequalities, particularly through biases that are not easily discernible. Such biases are embedded in the technical and social structures of artificial intelligence systems, making them difficult to detect. These biases challenge the concept of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI), which recognizes diversity as the acknowledgment of individual differences, equity as fairness and equal access, and inclusion as the value placed on all participants. This study argues that fairness in artificial intelligence systems cannot be achieved by focusing solely on their technical aspects, necessitating a holistic approach. This study employs a two-phase mixed-methods design. Phase 1 applies computational content analysis to 360 occupational narratives generated by ChatGPT across four countries (Canada, Germany, India, and Bangladesh) using gender-neutral prompts to examine whether professions are predominantly associated with one gender and whether these patterns remain consistent across regions. Phase 2 examines the extent to which students recognize potential bias in AI, their trust in AI for consequential decision-making, and how these perceptions relate to themes in EDI and AI ethics scholarship. By combining output-level bias analysis with user perception data, this study identifies the empirical foundations necessary for future EDI-AI co-design frameworks, outlining the sociotechnical dimensions that such frameworks must address to be effective.

papers.title: Proxy Metrics Can Hide Downstream Collapse: A Case Study on Compressed Cellular Segmentation
papers.abstract: Post-training compression of vision models is commonly screened using output-level proxies such as normalized RMSE (NRMSE), cosine similarity, and flow angular error. We evaluated post-training quantization of Cellpose-SAM, a promptless Segment-Anything model for cellular instance segmentation, on a stratified 245-field panel spanning BBBC038, BBBC039, and NIST iPSC images across density regimes. These proxies failed to reliably predict downstream mask retention under activation quantization. Angular error saturated at 90{\deg} from A8 through A2, while cosine and NRMSE preserved rank-order information without providing an interpretable acceptance threshold. At W8A8-cal-QDQ, cosine similarity was 0.944 despite 89/245 empty masks; moreover, performance varied sharply by modality, with BBBC039 yielding 0/47 empty masks versus 63/99 for NIST iPSC fields at the same proxy footprint. Across five modality-density strata, cosine similarity and empty-mask rate showed weak rank agreement (\r{ho}=~0.3), with the highest-cosine stratum producing the second-worst downstream outcome. Below A8, all modalities collapsed to 245/245 empty fields. By contrast, ternary weight quantization produced a 12.08x storage reduction and was correctly identified as catastrophic by the proxies. These results show that FP32-referenced output proxies are insufficient as standalone acceptance criteria for promptless dense-prediction models; compression should instead be validated against downstream retention stratified by deployment-relevant imaging conditions.

papers.title: How Small Can a Single Shor Run Be? Limits and Constructions for secp256k1
papers.abstract: Most resource estimates for breaking secp256k1 with Shor's algorithm describe one long run per attempt, and the spacetime volume of that run, its peak number of logical qubits times its Toffoli count, sets its logical-error budget. Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff shrinks each run by using more runs, but how far it can shrink the largest run, and at what circuit cost, has not been determined. We minimize the volume of the largest run while every key is recovered with probability at least 0.99, within ten times the total volume of three runs of H\"aner et al.\ and $2^{40}$ classical operations. We prove that a linear run fixed in advance, which starts its group register at a point and discards its label, reveals at most $\log_2(1+(|S|-1)/r)$ bits about a uniform key, where $|S|$ counts its exponent values and $r$ is the group order. With generic post-processing and the baseline's window costs, splitting alone then shrinks the largest run at most 1.86 times within the budget. To gain more, we make each exponent bit cheaper with windows that share one table point among exponent values related by six symmetries of the curve, on a point-addition core borrowed from the ECDSA.Fail leaderboard. One random scalar and one random start per run give every approximate addition uniform operands, and a bound on each run's outcomes certifies, for every key, a decoder that discards flagged runs. We count every Toffoli gate and every qubit of every run, and each configuration solved all 563 of its pre-registered simulated trials on secp256k1. The best one shrinks the largest run 3.87 times at 8.79 times the baseline's total volume, against 2.81 times for Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff on the same core, and its run is at least 2.6 times smaller than every design of Initio Intelligence.

papers.title: A Self-Organizing Swarm Control Model for Underwater Robots Based on Turing-Type Reaction-Diffusion Principles
papers.abstract: In underwater environments, Global Positioning System (GPS) signals and high-speed radio communication are unavailable, and severe constraints exist on communication bandwidth and visibility; consequently, applying conventional swarm formation methods, such as the Boids model, which require the relative positions and velocity vectors of neighboring vehicles, is difficult. This study proposes a decentralized swarm control model that operates without a leader or absolute coordinates, relying solely on the number of received signals from two communication channels with different transmission ranges (inner and outer neighborhoods). The proposed model extends a cellular automaton model based on Turing pattern formation principles to continuous space and is grounded in the fundamental concept that swarms form as robots move toward regions of higher potential calculated from the difference in received signal counts. Specifically, stable behavior is determined through temporal averaging of potential values, hysteresis-based state evaluation, stepwise turning based on temporal differences, and vector composition with an external directional command. Two-dimensional simulation results demonstrated that autonomous swarm formation and control of swarm spatial dispersion via a morphological parameter are achievable, confirming robustness in maintaining swarms and high polarization even under communication dropouts where the communication success rate decreases to approximately 0.7.

papers.title: Net-Gain-Optimized Constellation Shaping for the 5G NR DFT-s-OFDM Uplink: Probabilistic, Geometric, and Joint Designs
papers.abstract: Constellation shaping improves the achievable information rate of coded modulation. On the single-carrier uplink waveform of 5G New Radio, discrete Fourier transform (DFT)- spread orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), the same shaping can also raise the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). A higher PAPR forces more power amplifier back- off and reduces the link budget. Prior work characterized this penalty for fixed probabilistically and geometrically shaped constellations, but did not turn the trade-off into a design objective. We optimize constellation shaping (CS) to maximize the net-gain, i.e., the sum of the communication gain and the PAPR gain, at the fixed spectral efficiency of 4 bits per channel use for 64-QAM. We apply it to probabilistic shaping (PS), geometric shaping (GS), and a joint scheme that combines both. As the coded block error rate cannot be evaluated inside a gradient loop, we use the achievable information rate as a surrogate for the communication performance and the PAPR surrogate as differentiable cost functions for the optimizer. The learned constellations are then validated on a complete DFT-s-OFDM link-level chain. Conventional Maxwell-Boltzmann PS yields a negative net-gain, but net-gain-aware optimization removes this deficit in every method. GS converts it into a substantial gain, as it not only improves the communication performance but also lowers the PAPR below the uniform 64-QAM reference, achieving the largest net-gain among the CS methods studied.

papers.title: MAQR: Lightweight Memory-Aware Q-Routing for Fresh Status Delivery in Multi-Hop IoBNTs
papers.abstract: This paper proposes memory-aware Q-routing (MAQR) for fresh status delivery over history-dependent molecular links in multi-hop Internet of Bio-Nano Things (IoBNT) networks. Repeated transmissions leave residual molecules, making link reliability history-dependent and fixed routing inefficient. Each link is calibrated from a spatial Markov model and approximated by three nonnegative decay modes. The resulting reduced memory state and packet bit composition provide an instantaneous link-success estimate. MAQR combines quantized memory and reliability descriptors with packet age, queue occupancy, and molecule reserve in a lightweight partially observable Q-routing heuristic. It is trained offline and requires only reduced-state updates and Q-table lookup during deployment. Across five independent training pairs and 20 shared evaluation seeds, MAQR reduces mean AoI by 46.9 % relative to memory-blind Q-routing at 0.30 packets/slot while improving molecular efficiency. Frozen-policy sweeps further show comparable performance under weak memory and an increasing MAQR advantage as channel memory strengthens.

papers.title: Observable Spectral Framework for Noisy Amplitude Amplification: Stopping Stability and Correction
papers.abstract: Stopping rules for noisy amplitude amplification often rely on channel-specific success-probability formulas, limiting their transfer across noise mechanisms. We develop an observable spectral framework for stationary noisy standard amplitude amplification with a known ideal success fraction, under explicit leading-mode, spectral-separation, and residual-control conditions. Within this class, the first amplification lobe has a damped-oscillatory leading component and a bounded non-leading contribution. We derive how frequency shift, damping, and observable phase offset displace the leading peak, and establish sampled-gap criteria for retaining the ideal integer stopping depth, certifying recalibration, or selecting a robust candidate window. In single-target Grover search, frequency and damping errors have stopping-coordinate sensitivities proportional to the search-space size, whereas phase offsets scale with its square root; residual modes can independently reverse the ordering of neighbouring depths. Analytical constructions, circuit simulations, finite-shot inference, and calibration-derived device-like trajectories examine these predictions and their operational limits. For a 64-element search, an a posteriori sampled-set check selects depth five over six, with success probability increasing from 0.595 to 0.626. The resulting theory links observable spectral dynamics to conditional integer stopping guarantees without requiring a separate microscopic channel solution.

papers.title: FliX: Flipped-Indexing for Scalable GPU Queries and Updates
papers.abstract: GPU concurrent data structures (CDSs) achieve very high read-only throughput, but fully dynamic updates on GPU-resident data remain challenging. Ordered CDSs (e.g., B-trees and LSM-trees) route operations through an index layer to a data layer of buckets. Maintaining and traversing that index under updates causes contention, warp divergence, and memory overhead. Hash tables avoid this cost but lose range and successor queries. We present FliX, a comparison-based flipped indexing strategy that eliminates the index layer. Instead of assigning a warp to each operation, FliX assigns a warp to each bucket. Each bucket then binary-searches a sorted batch for its operations, so one search replaces many index traversals and updates become simple. FliX reduces query latency by up to 6.5x versus a leading GPU B-tree and 1.5x versus the leading GPU LSM-tree. It delivers 4x higher throughput per memory footprint than ordered competitors and over 8x higher insertion throughput than the closest fully dynamic ordered baseline. It also matches or beats unordered GPU hash tables on point queries and deletions, so its ordering support comes at virtually no cost. FliX also supports fully concurrent execution of queries and updates. In an update-heavy mixed workload, it achieves 4.42x the throughput of a GPU hash table and 11.39s the throughput of a B-tree. Our results suggest that FliX can support fast queries, efficient updates, and memory reclamation on fully GPU-resident data while maintaining key order and allowing fully concurrent execution.
